Based on my observations, I have the following recommendations:

Remove the mixing shaft from the pipe feeding the Hopper. Since the current product does not contain flavoring, I recommend removing the shaft. Dark chocolate is thicker and tends to stick to the shaft, which can gradually build up and cause the pipe to become clogged. I recommend keeping the shaft visible and hanging in a designated location so it can be reinstalled when flavored chocolate is used.
Confirm the maximum temperature setting with Candon. According to the graph currently being followed, the tempering machine is set to 25.5°C. We should ask Candon what the maximum allowable temperature is for this process.
Review the operator’s temperature adjustments according to the OPL. According to the OPL, operators can adjust both the water temperature and the chocolate temperature to achieve the desired results based on the graph. We should ensure these adjustments are made according to the established procedure.

These are my recommendations to help prevent pipe blockage and maintain proper chocolate flow and tempering conditions.

I am 95% confident that the mixing shaft is causing the blockage as chocolate passes through the pipe over time.
